sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Ikea hacking is what we've been doing.
sentences.zh: 宜家改装正是我们一直在做的事情。

sentences.en: And this is friend of the show, Sean Cole.
sentences.zh: 这位是节目的老朋友肖恩·科尔。

sentences.en: And yes, he said Ikea hacking.
sentences.zh: 没错，他刚才说的是宜家改装。

sentences.en: I feel good about it.
sentences.zh: 我感觉这挺不错的。

sentences.en: It feels a little bit subversive and a little bit bourgeois.
sentences.zh: 它既带有一点颠覆性，又带有一点资产阶级气息。

sentences.en: It's like being a punk member of the mainstream.
sentences.zh: 就像是主流当中的朋克一员。

sentences.en: Given that our audience is, you know, our audience, you've probably heard of Ikea hacking.
sentences.zh: 考虑到我们的听众就是那种听众，你们大概也听说过宜家改装。

sentences.en: It's the practice of buying stuff from Ikea and then re-engineering it, hacking it,
sentences.zh: 这就是从宜家买东西，然后进行重新设计、改装，

sentences.en: into customized, more functional, and often just way better designed stuff.
sentences.zh: 把它变成定制的、功能更强的，而且通常设计好得多的东西。

sentences.en: In Sean's case, that stuff is three five-foot-high shelves.
sentences.zh: 在肖恩的这个例子里，那些东西是三个五英尺高的书架。

sentences.en: Sean has decided upon the Calyx variety, plus two very heavy wooden doors from Home Depot,
sentences.zh: 肖恩选定了卡莱克斯系列，再加上两扇来自全美家得宝的很重的木门，

sentences.en: all of which he is drilling and screwing and bolting together into one big, beautiful, queen-sized,
sentences.zh: 他正在把这些东西全部钻孔、用螺丝和螺栓固定在一起，拼成一张巨大、漂亮、双人尺寸的

sentences.en: Frankenstein storage bed to cure his basement-less New York City existence.
sentences.zh: 科学怪人式储物床，来拯救他在纽约市没有地下室的生存状态。

sentences.en: We are finishing the construction of the third Calyx shelf.
sentences.zh: 我们正在完成第三个卡莱克斯书架的组装。

sentences.en: We've become expert Calyx assemblers.
sentences.zh: 我们已经成了熟练的卡莱克斯组装专家。

sentences.en: The locus of the Ikea hacking movement is a website called IkeaHackers.net.
sentences.zh: 宜家改装运动的中心是一个叫做IkeaHackers.net的网站。

sentences.en: It's a showcase for those who would trick out their Calyxes, their Arkelstorps, their Flardfuls.
sentences.zh: 它是那些想要魔改自己的卡莱克斯、阿克尔斯托普、弗拉德富尔的人的展示平台。

sentences.en: They can both gather tips from other hackers and, more importantly, boast pictures of their own hacks
sentences.zh: 他们既可以从其他改装者那里收集小贴士，更重要的是，还能晒出自己改装作品的照片，

sentences.en: and even a step-by-step guide to how they made them.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有他们如何制作的分步指南。

sentences.en: IkeaHackers.net has been in the news a lot lately, and not for happy reasons.
sentences.zh: IkeaHackers.net最近上了很多新闻，而且可不是什么开心的原因。

sentences.en: You might have read those stories online.
sentences.zh: 你们可能在网上读过那些报道。

sentences.en: We're going to get into all that later, but first, I wanted to introduce you to my hacker partner in crime,
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会深入探讨这些，但首先，我想向大家介绍我的改装同谋，

sentences.en: Jonathan Bean.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·比恩。

sentences.en: He's an assistant professor at Bucknell University.
sentences.zh: 他是巴克内尔大学的助理教授。

sentences.en: Back in 2009, he co-wrote a serious academic paper about Ikea hacking with Daniela Rosner,
sentences.zh: 早在2009年，他与丹妮拉·罗斯纳合写了一篇关于宜家改装的严肃学术论文，

sentences.en: who now teaches design at the University of Washington.
sentences.zh: 丹妮拉现在在华盛顿大学教设计。

sentences.en: And they got interested in part because of how bendable the term Ikea hacking is.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以对此产生兴趣，部分原因在于“宜家改装”这个词的弹性实在太大了。

sentences.en: Here's Jonathan.
sentences.zh: 有请乔纳森。

sentences.en: There was so much when you scratch the surface about what Ikea hacking could be.
sentences.zh: 当你深入探究宜家改装可能是什么时，内容实在是太丰富了。

sentences.en: It could be anything from, I bought this shelf at Ikea and it was an inch too long for my closet,
sentences.zh: 它可以是从“我在宜家买了这个书架，但比我的衣柜长了一英寸，

sentences.en: so I cut an inch off of it.
sentences.zh: 所以我把它切短了一英寸”这样的事。

sentences.en: Or it could be where you just take, say, a salad bowl and make it into a light.
sentences.zh: 或者也可以是你拿一个沙拉碗，把它做成一盏灯。

sentences.en: And this is Daniela.
sentences.zh: 这位是丹妮拉。

sentences.en: Right, that's not even actually changing the object itself.
sentences.zh: 没错，这实际上甚至没有改变物品本身。

sentences.en: It's just changing its use.
sentences.zh: 它只是改变了物品的用途。

sentences.en: And at the other end of the spectrum, an artist named Sondra von Wussel did a very provocative work of art,
sentences.zh: 而在光谱的另一端，一位名叫桑德拉·冯·乌塞尔的艺术家创作了一件非常挑衅的艺术品，

sentences.en: which is an Ikea chair reconfigured to look like a stirrup from a gynecologist's office.
sentences.zh: 那是一把被重新配置成看起来像妇科诊所检查蹬具的宜家椅子。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: And both of these things fall under the rubric of Ikea hacking.
sentences.zh: 这两类事情都属于宜家改装的范畴。

sentences.en: That's a really wide rubric.
sentences.zh: 这个范畴可真够广泛的。

sentences.en: And now, please put your hands over your children's ears for 20 seconds.
sentences.zh: 现在，请捂住你孩子们的耳朵20秒钟。

sentences.en: I really like the Ikea love toy as another example where you take...
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢宜家情趣玩具这个例子，你可以拿……

sentences.en: Ikea love toy?
sentences.zh: 宜家情趣玩具？

sentences.en: A love toy made of the Ormsong shoe trees and an Ikea product that's the milk frothing device.
sentences.zh: 一个由奥姆松鞋撑和一个宜家打奶器产品制成的轻量级情趣玩具。

sentences.en: So taking those together and making a little vibrator.
sentences.zh: 把这两者结合起来，就制作出了一个小型振动器。

sentences.en: This is a much racier interview than I was expecting it to be.
sentences.zh: 这次采访比我预期的要劲爆得多。

sentences.en: And the Hakkarati aren't just diverse in terms of their sensibility.
sentences.zh: 而且“哈卡拉蒂”不仅在审美品味上呈现多样化。

sentences.en: They're diverse in the most basic way possible.
sentences.zh: 他们在最基础的层面上也是多元的。

sentences.en: You see hacks posted from all over this country and from Australia, Russia, Israel, Dubai.
sentences.zh: 你看到发布的改装作品来自这个国家的各地，还有澳大利亚、俄罗斯、以色列、迪拜。

sentences.en: Someone posted a hack that's a French country house library in an actual French country house.
sentences.zh: 有人发布了一个改装作品，是在真正的法国乡村别墅里打造的一间法国乡村别墅图书馆。

sentences.en: He used 60 billion Benno bookcases and he has these before and after pictures and explained all how he did it.
sentences.zh: 他用了600亿个贝诺书柜，发布了这些前后对比照片，并解释了他是如何做到的。

sentences.en: Because everything's exactly the same at Ikea, no matter where you are,
sentences.zh: 因为无论你在哪里，宜家的所有东西都完全一样，

sentences.en: it sort of lowers the barriers to recreating something.
sentences.zh: 这在一定程度上降低了重新创造某些东西的门槛。

sentences.en: Because this is the thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: Say I wanted to teach you, Roman, how to build a workbench.
sentences.zh: 假设我想教你，罗曼，如何建造一个工作台。

sentences.en: But you live in Germany and I live in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但你住在德国，而我住在美国。

sentences.en: If you go and buy a stud, a wood stud at a Home Depot in the U.S., it's going to be an inch and a half by three and a half inches.
sentences.zh: 如果你去美国一家家得宝买一根木方，尺寸将是一英寸半乘以三英寸半。

sentences.en: If you go and buy a wood stud at Bauhaus, which is a German home improvement store, it's going to be a different size.
sentences.zh: 如果你去德国一家名为包豪斯的家居建材商店买一根木方，尺寸就会完全不同。

sentences.en: Wait, tell me I'm not dreaming and he just said that there's a German home improvement store called Bauhaus.
sentences.zh: 等等，告诉我这不是在做梦，他刚才说有一家德国家居建材店叫包豪斯？

sentences.en: Yes, but it's actually Swiss.
sentences.zh: 是的，但它其实是瑞士的。

sentences.en: That's so fantastic.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Ikea, in spite of itself, is the great leveler.
sentences.zh: 宜家在违背其本意的情况下，成为了伟大的拉平者。

sentences.en: And it's that very homogeneity, that McDonald's-like sameness from place to place to place.
sentences.zh: 正是这种同质性，那种从一个地方到另一个地方都像麦当劳一样的千篇一律，

sentences.en: That's what's allowing this global community of hackers to thrive.
sentences.zh: 才使得这个全球改装者社区能够蓬勃发展。

sentences.en: So if I posted an Ikea hack in Boston and someone in the Netherlands saw it,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我在波士顿发布了一个宜家改装作品，而荷兰有人看到了，

sentences.en: they could probably reproduce it using the pieces at their local store, much like a Lego kit.
sentences.zh: 他们很可能会利用当地商店的零件复制出来，就像乐高积木一样。

sentences.en: Make no mistake, the actual posts themselves, showing your work, that's a huge part of this whole thing.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，实际发布的作品本身，展示你的成果，这是整个事件中非常巨大的一部分。

sentences.en: I think that there is something to this feeling of recognition.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种被认可的感觉是有一定道理的。

sentences.en: Like, you're not creative unless you're recognized as being creative.
sentences.zh: 就像，除非你被公认为具有创造力，否则你就不算有创造力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: If Ikea is hacked in a forest, does it make a sound?
sentences.zh: 如果森林里有一个宜家被改装了，它会发出声音吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Hey dolls, it's Theodore here, and I have officially done my first Ikea hack.
sentences.zh: 嗨，宝贝们，我是西奥多，我正式完成了我的第一个宜家改装。

sentences.en: I'm going to show you how I'm going to do an Ikea hack.
sentences.zh: 我来向大家展示我是如何进行宜家改装的。

sentences.en: My first Ikea hack.
sentences.zh: 我的第一个宜家改装。

sentences.en: So we've got an Ikea piece that we're going to be modifying.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有一个准备要改造的宜家单品。

sentences.en: And as you might expect, there's a lot of this kind of hacking and showing and telling on YouTube, too.
sentences.zh: 正如你所料，YouTube上也有很多这种改装、展示和讲解的内容。

sentences.en: By now, the search term shouldn't be too mysterious.
sentences.zh: 到了现在，这个搜索词应该已经不怎么神秘了。

sentences.en: Ikea hack.
sentences.zh: 宜家改装。

sentences.en: And we are checking out her beautiful Ikea transformation pieces, which I like to call them.
sentences.zh: 我们正在查看她那些美丽的宜家改造作品，我喜欢这样称呼它们。

sentences.en: You call them...
sentences.zh: 你管它们叫……

sentences.en: Hack jobs.
sentences.zh: 粗劣改装。

sentences.en: Hack jobs.
sentences.zh: 粗劣改装。

sentences.en: I'll show you how to customize your Ikea Tulsa armchair.
sentences.zh: 我来教你如何定制你的宜家塔尔萨扶手椅。

sentences.en: I'm going to go measure how far my elbows are up in relation to this desk.
sentences.zh: 我要去测量一下我的手肘相对于这个桌子的高度。

sentences.en: Now let's put on the marble contact paper onto the top of the table.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们把大理石纹接触纸贴在桌子顶部。

sentences.en: Okay, and there we have our installed six-inch cabinet.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们安装好的六英寸橱柜就在那里了。

sentences.en: So now we have a really cool shoe locker.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们有了一个非常酷的鞋柜。

sentences.en: You don't know if it's from Ikea.
sentences.zh: 你根本不知道它是不是来自宜家。

sentences.en: It could be.
sentences.zh: 它可能是。

sentences.en: It might not be.
sentences.zh: 也可能不是。

sentences.en: For $44 worth of parts from Ikea...
sentences.zh: 只需花44美元买宜家的零件……

sentences.en: But why aren't they, I mean, if they're good enough to do some, frankly, pretty remarkable things with these materials, like,
sentences.zh: 但他们为什么不，我是说，既然他们有能力用这些材料做出坦率说相当卓越的东西，比如，

sentences.en: why aren't they just going and buying raw lumber and screws and nails and hammering together something maybe more lasting and less pressboard-y?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们不去买些原木、螺丝和钉子，敲打出更持久、不那么像密度板的东西呢？

sentences.en: Well, they're not just hacking the materials, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们不只是在改装材料，对吧？

sentences.en: They're hacking Ikea.
sentences.zh: 他们在改装宜家。

sentences.en: They're hacking the brand.
sentences.zh: 他们在改装这个品牌。

sentences.en: They're hacking what that brand actually symbolizes beyond just the stores.
sentences.zh: 他们在改装这个品牌在商店之外实际象征的意义。

sentences.en: Or put another way, to quote Danielle and Jonathan, they're mocking the modularity of Ikea, saying this stuff is so Tinker Toy, I can mix and mash up the hell out of it.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，用丹妮拉和乔纳森的话来引用，他们在嘲弄宜家的模块化，说这些东西就像拼插玩具，我可以狠狠地把它们混合拼凑起来。

sentences.en: And it also goes back to that homogeneity, right?
sentences.zh: 这也回到了那种同质性，对吧？

sentences.en: That if this is the McDonald's of furniture, I'm going to go against the grain and make a double, triple, extra pickle Big Mac with no middle bun in it.
sentences.zh: 如果这是家具界的麦当劳，我要反其道而行之，做一个双层、三层、加酸黄瓜且中间没有面包胚的巨无霸。

sentences.en: Right, it's part of your identity at that point.
sentences.zh: 没错，到了那个地步，它成了你身份的一部分。

sentences.en: You're saying I'm a person who transforms things.
sentences.zh: 你在表达：我是一个能够改造事物的人。

sentences.en: But this is where it gets even more complicated, according to Jonathan.
sentences.zh: 但据乔纳森所说，事情在这里变得更加复杂了。

sentences.en: Within that group of people who wanted to completely transform something, some of them really wanted to maintain the Ikea aesthetic.
sentences.zh: 在那些想要彻底改造某物的人群中，有些人真的只想保持宜家的美学。

sentences.en: So they would say, well, this is something we want to say that could have come from Ikea but didn't.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会说，好吧，这是我们想要表达的东西，它本可以来自宜家，但实际上并没有。

sentences.en: So there's a sort of sense of, sure, you want to express yourself, but you're also trying to sort of outdo the doer.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一种感觉，当然，你想表达自己，但你其实也试图超越那个创造者。

sentences.en: Like you're trying to outwit Ikea, right?
sentences.zh: 就像你想智胜宜家一样，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Out Ikea, Ikea.
sentences.zh: 比宜家更宜家。

sentences.en: All right, now we're going to lay the shelves down on their sides in a way that Ikea did not intend.
sentences.zh: 好了，现在我们要把书架侧放过来，以一种宜家原本没有设想过的方式。

sentences.en: We now rejoin this Ikea hack already in progress.
sentences.zh: 我们现在继续回到这个已经在进行中的宜家改装项目。

sentences.en: To catch everyone up, we have built three Kalex shelves from Ikea.
sentences.zh: 为了让大家跟上进度，我们已经组装好了三个宜家的卡莱克斯书架。

sentences.en: We've laid them down on their sides in a kind of view.
sentences.zh: 我们把它们侧着放，形成了一种视觉效果。

sentences.en: It's like my bed is a whale skeleton lying on its side, and you're going to be putting stuff in the ribcage of the skeleton.
sentences.zh: 就像我的床是一具侧躺着的鲸鱼骨架，而你要把东西放进骨架的胸腔里。

sentences.en: That's what my bed is going to be like.
sentences.zh: 我的床就是这个样子的。

sentences.en: And we're going to put doors, really heavy doors, on top of the shelves as where I'm going to lay down and go to sleepy by.
sentences.zh: 我们打算在书架顶部放上门，非常重的门，那将是我躺下来睡觉的地方。

sentences.en: You sound like an insane person.
sentences.zh: 听起来你像个疯子。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: You're like Aquaman standing on top of a wild marine creature.
sentences.zh: 你就像是站在野生海洋生物背上的海王。

sentences.en: But this is what it's like.
sentences.zh: 但这就是它的感觉。

sentences.en: It's like taming, you know.
sentences.zh: 就像驯服一样，你知道的。

sentences.en: Like taming the most placid beast in the known universe, an Ikea shelf on its side.
sentences.zh: 就像驯服已知宇宙中最温顺的野兽——一个侧放的宜家书架。

sentences.en: No, but this is what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 不，但这就是我想说的。

sentences.en: It isn't placid.
sentences.zh: 它可一点都不温顺。

sentences.en: It's us that is usually the placid.
sentences.zh: 通常是我们比较温顺。

sentences.en: Okay, this is the best part, actually.
sentences.zh: 好吧，其实这才是最棒的部分。

sentences.en: We're about to drill unsanctioned holes into a piece of Ikea furniture.
sentences.zh: 我们即将在一件宜家家具上钻下未经批准的孔。

sentences.en: You're not going to be able to take it back.
sentences.zh: 你可就没法退货了。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: You want to have at it?
sentences.zh: 你想来试试吗？

sentences.en: Oh, actually, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，其实，好啊。

sentences.en: May I do the honors?
sentences.zh: 我可以效劳吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So why is this your favorite part?
sentences.zh: 那为什么这是你最喜欢的部分？

sentences.en: I mean, I think that it's just that for the longest time, you know, you're told that drilling holes where they're not supposed to go is destructive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得很简单，很长一段时间以来，你知道的，大家都跟你说在不该钻孔的地方钻孔是一种破坏。

sentences.en: And wrong.
sentences.zh: 而且是不对的。

sentences.en: And we were doing that.
sentences.zh: 而我们当时正在那样做。

sentences.en: And it's still transgressive and you're crossing a boundary.
sentences.zh: 这依然具有越轨性，你在跨越一条界限。

sentences.en: But it's not destruction anymore.
sentences.zh: 但它不再是破坏了。

sentences.en: It's creation.
sentences.zh: 这是创造。

sentences.en: You know, it felt like for once I wasn't just saying, what's out there?
sentences.zh: 你知道，感觉有那么一次，我不仅仅是在说，外面有什么？

sentences.en: You know, which one on the menu do I want?
sentences.zh: 你知道，菜单上的哪一个是我想要的？

sentences.en: We were making what we wanted.
sentences.zh: 我们在制造我们想要的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, but you were still shopping at Ikea.
sentences.zh: 对，但你当时还在宜家购物。

sentences.en: True.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Well, it's interesting Ikea's response to this, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，宜家对此事的反应很有趣，对吧？

sentences.en: It's not to shut down Ikea hackers.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有关停宜家改装网（Ikea hackers）。

sentences.en: Again, this is Daniela Rosner, who co-wrote that Ikea hacking paper.
sentences.zh: 再次说明，这位是丹妮拉·罗丝纳（Daniela Rosner），她合著了那篇关于宜家改装的论文。

sentences.en: There's a lot more almost support for hacking within the corporate world than there was, you know, five or six years ago.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，现在企业内部对改装的支持，比五六年前要多得多。

sentences.en: And I think part of that is corporations seeing that this adds to the process of kind of buying and recognizing the products.
sentences.zh: 我想部分原因在于，企业看到这促进了购买和认可产品的过程。

sentences.en: And yes, this is the moment in the story where we do the ironic tape-to-tape juxtaposition.
sentences.zh: 没错，这就是故事里我们用讽刺的磁带剪辑手法进行对比的时刻。

sentences.en: Maestro?
sentences.zh: 乐队指挥？

sentences.en: Earlier this week, Swedish flat pack furniture manufacturer Ikea dealt a massive blow to the long-running fan blog IkeaHackers.net.
sentences.zh: 本周早些时候，瑞典平板家具制造商宜家对运营长久的粉丝博客 IkeaHackers.net 进行了沉重打击。

sentences.en: According to a blog post published by founder Jules Yap, the site was issued a cease and desist order in March.
sentences.zh: 根据创始人朱尔斯·叶（Jules Yap）发布的博客文章，该网站在三月份收到了停止侵权警告函。

sentences.en: This is the news that we alluded to at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在开头暗示的消息。

sentences.en: Around the same time that Sean and Jonathan were hacking together his bed, unbeknownst to them,
sentences.zh: 就在肖恩和乔纳森一起改装他的床时，在他们不知情的情况下，

sentences.en: a brand protection company wrote to the queen bee of Ikea Hackdom, the woman who runs IkeaHackers.net, Jules Yap.
sentences.zh: 一家品牌保护公司给宜家改装界的蜂王、运营 IkeaHackers.net 的朱尔斯·叶发了信。

sentences.en: Jules isn't her real first name.
sentences.zh: 朱尔斯不是她的真实名。

sentences.en: The letter basically said that Ikea was not amused, and that if Jules didn't stop operating her website the way she was, she could be in big trouble.
sentences.zh: 这封信基本上是说宜家很不高兴，如果朱尔斯不按要求停止运营她的网站，她可能会陷入大麻烦。

sentences.en: Hey, Jules.
sentences.zh: 嘿，朱尔斯。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm good.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: It wasn't until the news broke about the cease and desist letter that Jules agreed to talk to me.
sentences.zh: 直到关于停止侵权函的新闻爆出后，朱尔斯才同意和我交谈。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She lives in Malaysia, and we talked by Skype.
sentences.zh: 她住在马来西亚，我们通过 Skype 进行了交谈。

sentences.en: Before we got down to business, I was just curious how she thought up the site.
sentences.zh: 在进入正题之前，我很好奇她是怎么想出这个网站的点子的。

sentences.en: So I was checking out a few Home Deco websites, and I found a few IkeaHacks scattered around on the internet.
sentences.zh: 当时我在浏览一些家居装饰网站，发现互联网上散落着一些宜家改装案例。

sentences.en: And then that was when I thought, how great it would be if I could see all these hacks in one place.
sentences.zh: 然后我就想，如果能把所有这些改装案例集中在一个地方，那该多好啊。

sentences.en: And that was when, ta-da, the light bulbs just went on, and I knew I had to start it.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，哗啦，灵感乍现，我知道我必须创办它。

sentences.en: So that was in 2006, and for some reason only this year, 2014, March 12th to be precise, did Jules get an email...
sentences.zh: 那是 2006 年的事，不知为何，直到今年——准确地说是 2014 年 3 月 12 日，朱尔斯才收到一封电子邮件……

sentences.en: ...with the subject line, IkeaHackers, notification of violation of trademark rights.
sentences.zh: ……主题是“宜家改装网，侵犯商标权通知”。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So I felt my blood drain, literally.
sentences.zh: 当时我真的感觉血都快流干了。

sentences.en: You know, it was scary.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，太吓人了。

sentences.en: So what did they want her to do?
sentences.zh: 那他们想让她做什么？

sentences.en: Hand over the domain name, stop using the Ikea trademark or anything trademarked by Ikea,
sentences.zh: 交出域名，停止使用宜家商标或宜家拥有商标权的任何东西，

sentences.en: which I think means even pictures of the furniture, and she'd have to close down her Twitter and Facebook accounts too,
sentences.zh: 我想这甚至意味着家具的照片，她还必须关闭推特和脸书账号，

sentences.en: and all the social media stuff.
sentences.zh: 以及所有社交媒体的东西。

sentences.en: The thing that's ironic about this, the thing that I didn't understand right away,
sentences.zh: 这件事讽刺的地方在于，我一开始没有明白的地方，

sentences.en: was that Jules loves Ikea.
sentences.zh: 其实是朱尔斯非常喜欢宜家。

sentences.en: I mean, she's just a huge fan.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她简直是个超级粉丝。

sentences.en: I am, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Super fan.
sentences.zh: 超级粉丝。

sentences.en: It strikes me that it's like meeting a celebrity that you've always really loved,
sentences.zh: 这给我的感觉就像是见到了你一直非常喜爱的名人，

sentences.en: and like that celebrity is really mean to you in some way.
sentences.zh: 而那个名人在某种程度上对你非常刻薄。

sentences.en: Yes, yeah, that's close, you know.
sentences.zh: 对的，没错，差不多就是这样。

sentences.en: I just felt like after that, I had been given a restraining order by the celebrity.
sentences.zh: 我只觉得在那之后，我被这位名人发了限制令。

sentences.en: After Jules announced on her website that big changes might be coming to Ikea hackers,
sentences.zh: 在朱尔斯在网站上宣布宜家改装网可能会迎来重大变化之后，

sentences.en: the story went viral.
sentences.zh: 这个故事在网上疯传。

sentences.en: People were pretty pissed off.
sentences.zh: 大家都很生气。

sentences.en: Corey Doctorow, who blogs on Boing Boing, famously called the cease and desist letter,
sentences.zh: 在 Boing Boing 上写博客的科里·多克托罗（Corey Doctorow）曾有一句名言，他把这封停止侵权函称为

sentences.en: quote,
sentences.zh: 引述道，

sentences.en: steaming bullshit, end quote.
sentences.zh: 纯属放屁”，引文结束。

sentences.en: But at this point, Jules was pretty much resigned.
sentences.zh: 但到了这个时候，朱尔斯已经基本上认命了。

sentences.en: She thought the best thing she could do was just to comply and then transfer the hacks over to another site,
sentences.zh: 她认为自己能做的最好的事情就是照办，然后把改装案例转移到另一个网站上，

sentences.en: which didn't have Ikea's name on it.
sentences.zh: 那个网站没有宜家的名字。

sentences.en: If nothing else, she was just grateful that so many people reacted so strongly to the news.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，她只是很感激有这么多人对这个消息做出如此强烈的反应。

sentences.en: So it was on a Friday night that I made the announcement.
sentences.zh: 所以我是在一个周五晚上发布了公告。

sentences.en: And the following week, I received a call from Ikea.
sentences.zh: 接下来的星期，我接到了宜家的电话。

sentences.en: From whom at Ikea?
sentences.zh: 宜家的谁？

sentences.en: A guy named Anders Westney.
sentences.zh: 一个叫安德斯·维斯特尼（Anders Westney）的人。

sentences.en: I hope I'm saying that right.
sentences.zh: 希望我没念错他的名字。

sentences.en: He's with the business side of things as opposed to the legal side.
sentences.zh: 他是负责商业事务的，而不是法务部门的。

sentences.en: He was saying that, well, the lawyers are there to do their job, you know.
sentences.zh: 他说，律师嘛，就是做他们该做的工作。

sentences.en: And he also took a look at the letter of the cease and desist letter.
sentences.zh: 而且他也看了那封停止侵权函。

sentences.en: And he said that he didn't recognize Ikea in it.
sentences.zh: 他说他在里面没看到宜家的影子。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: He said that?
sentences.zh: 他这么说的？

sentences.en: Yes, he said that.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是这么说的。

sentences.en: As in, like, he didn't have the spirit of the brand, which is to make life better for everyone.
sentences.zh: 意思是，这不符合品牌的精神，也就是让每个人的生活都变得更好。

sentences.en: And to that end, he told Jules that they wanted to find another way forward
sentences.zh: 为此，他告诉朱尔斯，他们想寻找另一种前进的方式，

sentences.en: and try to figure out how they can resolve things to come to some agreement.
sentences.zh: 并试图弄清楚如何解决问题以达成某种协议。

sentences.en: Seriously, when he called me, I was totally speechless.
sentences.zh: 说实话，他打电话来的时候，我完全说不出话来。

sentences.en: I was like, uh, yeah, uh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我就像，呃，对，呃，对。

sentences.en: And, uh, but inside me, I was, like, screaming, yes, you know, like, I was, like, jumping, you know, if I could.
sentences.zh: 但是，我内心其实在尖叫，太棒了，如果可以的话，我甚至想跳起来。

sentences.en: Doing the Ikea dance.
sentences.zh: 跳起宜家之舞。

sentences.en: I was, like, crazy, you know.
sentences.zh: 我当时整个人都快疯了。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: And get this.
sentences.zh: 还有这个。

sentences.en: As we're releasing this podcast, Jules is visiting Sweden and Holland,
sentences.zh: 就在我们发布这期播客时，朱尔斯正在瑞典和荷兰访问，

sentences.en: meeting face-to-face with representatives of Ikea.
sentences.zh: 与宜家代表进行面对面会谈。

sentences.en: She's touring the concept center where their products are developed
sentences.zh: 她正在参观他们开发产品的概念中心，

sentences.en: and then visiting the very homeland where it all began.
sentences.zh: 然后还要造访这一切开始的发源地。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: It's like she's Charlie Bucket visiting Willy Wonka's chocolate factory.
sentences.zh: 这就像是查理·巴克特（Charlie Bucket）参观威利·旺卡（Willy Wonka）的巧克力工厂一样。

sentences.en: Yes, I am.
sentences.zh: 是的，就是这样。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: E.T.
sentences.zh: E.T.

sentences.en: go home.
sentences.zh: 回家吧。

sentences.en: I mean, do you get a sense that, um, Ikea would ever truly partner with Jules
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你觉得，呃……宜家有没有可能真的和朱尔斯合作，

sentences.en: and make her some sort of minister of hacking or whatever?
sentences.zh: 封她个什么改装大臣之类的职位？

sentences.en: I mean, what I've been saying is, like, I can't imagine Ikea could possibly endorse
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我一直以来的说法是，我无法想象宜家会认可

sentences.en: any individual hack or hacking on the whole.
sentences.zh: 任何个体的改装或整体的改装行为。

sentences.en: It's just too risky, you know.
sentences.zh: 这风险太大了。

sentences.en: I mean, if something goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果出了什么问题的话。

sentences.en: I mean, it would basically be sanctioning what amounts to a misuse of their products.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这基本上等于认可了对他们产品的错误使用。

sentences.en: Even though, I will say, that misuse feels wonderful.
sentences.zh: 尽管我要说的是，这种错误使用感觉太棒了。

sentences.en: I have to tell you, Jules, I, I, the feeling of hacking together my Ikea bed,
sentences.zh: 我必须告诉你，朱尔斯，我，我，一起改装我的宜家床的那种感觉，

sentences.en: well, I and Jonathan Bean, because it was really mostly him,
sentences.zh: 好吧，其实我和乔纳森·宾，因为主要都是他在弄，

sentences.en: but we, you know, created something.
sentences.zh: 但我们，你知道的，创造了一些东西。

sentences.en: And that thing that we created is now something that I sleep on every night.
sentences.zh: 我们创造的那东西现在成了我每天晚上睡觉的地方。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: It's just such a powerful feeling.
sentences.zh: 这真是一种强烈的感受。

sentences.en: There is actually a theory that, um, one of the reasons why Ikea is so successful
sentences.zh: 其实有一个理论，呃，宜家之所以如此成功的原因之一，

sentences.en: is because, uh, you have to make it yourself, as in, like, you have to assemble it yourself.
sentences.zh: 是因为，呃，你必须自己动手做，也就是说，你必须自己组装。

sentences.en: So it gives you a certain sense of accomplishment, or, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以它会带给你某种成就感，或者说，

sentences.en: I put together this billy bouquets or something, you know.
sentences.zh: 我组装了这个毕利（Billy）书柜之类的东西。

sentences.en: Um, so I think hacking is just taking it a level higher.
sentences.zh: 所以，我觉得改装只是把它提升到了一个更高的水平。

sentences.en: All right, this is the final touch.
sentences.zh: 好了，这是最后一步。

sentences.en: We're going to put the mattress onto my new Ikea bed.
sentences.zh: 我们要把床垫放到我的新宜家床上。

sentences.en: Does it fit?
sentences.zh: 放得下吗？

sentences.en: Does it fit?
sentences.zh: 放得下吗？

sentences.en: It fits!
sentences.zh: 放下了！

sentences.en: Oh, boy!
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪！

sentences.en: It's a bed!
sentences.zh: 这是一张床！

sentences.en: It's a bed!
sentences.zh: 这是一张床！

sentences.en: It's a real bed!
sentences.zh: 这是一张真正的床！

sentences.en: I'm not just a loser bachelor sleeping on the floor anymore.
sentences.zh: 我不再只是一个睡在地板上的失意单身汉了。

sentences.en: I'm in an actual bed!
sentences.zh: 我睡在真正的床上了！

sentences.en: Oh, boy!
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪！

sentences.en: Oh, boy!
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪！

sentences.en: I'm lying on my new bed.
sentences.zh: 我正躺在我的新床上。

sentences.en: It's so comfortable!
sentences.zh: 太舒服了！

sentences.en: He still sounds like a crazy person.
sentences.zh: 他听起来还是像个疯子。

sentences.en: One more thing to add here.
sentences.zh: 这里还要补充一件事。

sentences.en: We also wrote to Anders Wesny, the Ikea rep who reached out to Jules Yap, saying,
sentences.zh: 我们也写信给了安德斯·韦斯特尼，也就是联系了朱尔斯·叶的那个宜家代表，信中说，

sentences.en: and let's figure out a new way forward.
sentences.zh: 让我们找出一条新的前进道路吧。

sentences.en: He was very polite, but said that talking to us before talking to Jules would be putting
sentences.zh: 他非常礼貌，但表示在和朱尔斯谈话之前先和我们谈，那就是

sentences.en: the cart before the horse.
sentences.zh: 本末倒置了。

sentences.en: So, in short, no comment.
sentences.zh: 所以，简而言之，无可奉告。

sentences.en: We'll have to wait for an update on IkeaHackers.net.
sentences.zh: 我们得等 IkeaHackers.net 上的最新消息了。

sentences.en: Right, that's right.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: The steel's going to take its place.
sentences.zh: 钢材将会取代它的位置。

sentences.en: That way, we only have to buy two things instead of six.
sentences.zh: 这样，我们只需要买两样东西，而不是六样。

sentences.en: You are so smart.
sentences.zh: 你太聪明了。

sentences.en: You're hacking the hack.
sentences.zh: 你在改装这个改装方案。

sentences.en: Do you realize that you're hacking the hack?
sentences.zh: 你意识到你在改装这个改装方案吗？

sentences.en: That's what hacking is.
sentences.zh: 这就是改装的意义所在。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Sean Cole with Sam Greenspan, Katie Mingle, Avery
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》由肖恩·科尔（Sean Cole）与萨姆·格林斯潘（Sam Greenspan）、凯蒂·明格尔（Katie Mingle）、艾弗里·

sentences.en: Truffelman, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 特鲁夫曼（Truffelman）以及我，罗曼·马斯（Roman Mars）共同制作。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 local public radio KALW in San Francisco and produced out of
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 本地公共广播电台 KALW 的一个项目，制作工作室位于

sentences.zh: ArcSign，那里有一些由极精巧改装的 Expedit 书架，坐落于加利福尼亚州美丽的市中心

sentences.en: Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 奥克兰。

sentences.en: The full 99% Invisible experience isn't just this episode you're hearing.
sentences.zh: 完整的《99%隐形》体验不仅仅是你正在收听的这一集。

sentences.en: I post links to cool things and details about office hours and live shows on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 我会在脸书上发布酷炫玩意的链接，以及关于办公时间和直播节目的详情。

sentences.en: I also do that and, you know, make jokes on Twitter, at Roman Mars, along with our team
sentences.zh: 我也会在推特上发布这些内容，并顺便开开玩笑，账号是 @Roman Mars，我们的团队成员还有

sentences.en: Sam Listens, Katie Mingle, and Truffelman.
sentences.zh: 萨姆·利斯滕斯（Sam Listens）、凯蒂·明格尔和特鲁夫曼。

sentences.en: We're also on Tumblr, Instagram, Flickr, SoundCloud, and Spotify.
sentences.zh: 我们也在 Tumblr、Instagram、Flickr、SoundCloud 和 Spotify 上。

sentences.en: But you're always welcome at our place at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 但随时欢迎你访问我们的主页 99pi.org。
